record.title: Latent Compaction reports retrieval accuracy gains from document-specific test-time KV-cache training
record.summary: A 14 October arXiv preprint introduces Latent Compaction, which uses test-time training to optimize a compact, document-specific key–value cache while keeping model weights frozen. The authors report a highlighted RULER result of 96.7% accuracy at 32× compression versus 40.0% for KVZip+, and report broader gains on LongBench at stronger compression ratios across Qwen3 model sizes. The paper also states that text summarization outperforms Latent Compaction on RULER at the most aggressive ratios and that Phonebook Lookup accuracy approaches zero for all compressed methods at 64× and above. These are author-reported benchmark results. The evaluation counts logical KV pairs; it does not measure actual memory savings or inference speed.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Latent Compaction initializes a document-specific compact KV cache using reconstruction importance, teacher attention and key-space diversity, then trains cache entries in two stages to match full-cache attention and outputs. The base model weights remain frozen; the authors say training uses generic document prompts without downstream questions or answers.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors highlight a RULER result of 96.7% accuracy at 32× compression versus 40.0% for KVZip+. The paper’s Figure 1 compares Qwen3-1.7B on RULER and Phonebook Lookup. This is a reported benchmark result, not an independent reproduction.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper reports that on LongBench Latent Compaction exceeds text summarization across tested compression settings and KVZip+ at 16× and 32× across Qwen3-0.6B, 1.7B and 4B. It says the advantage is smaller at 4× and scores still decline as compression rises, leaving a gap to uncompressed models.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The authors explicitly state that their comparisons concern logical KV-pair budgets, not measured memory savings or inference-speed improvements. Their RULER discussion also reports that text summarization outperforms Latent Compaction at the most aggressive ratios and Phonebook Lookup approaches zero for all compressed methods at 64× and above.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The author repository is publicly accessible and lists implementation code under an MIT license. Repository availability is verified; this review did not run the code, download models, or independently reproduce the paper’s results.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of the reported retrieval gains was located or performed in this review.
Logical KV-pair counts do not establish physical memory reduction, actual throughput or latency; no serving measurement was performed in this review.
Document-specific cache training has preparation costs that may be amortized only when documents are reused; end-to-end economics under varied reuse rates remain unknown.

brief.importance_rationale: If independently replicated with real memory and latency measurements, document-specific optimization of compact KV state could materially change long-context inference choices; the score reflects potential impact in the stated regimes, not truth confidence.
limitations: All performance results are author-reported in a single preprint and were not independently reproduced.
The authors define compression using logical KV-pair budgets; physical memory usage and inference speed were not measured.

The reported advantage varies by benchmark and ratio: text summarization is stronger at the most aggressive RULER ratios, and Phonebook Lookup approaches zero accuracy for all compressed methods at 64× and above.
The highlighted 96.7% versus 40.0% comparison is a paper-selected result; broader transfer and operational performance require independent measurement.
The author repository was inspected for availability and license only; code, dependencies, model artifacts and data were not audited or executed.
brief.summary: A 14 October arXiv preprint introduces Latent Compaction, which uses test-time training to optimize a compact, document-specific key–value cache while keeping model weights frozen. The authors report a highlighted RULER result of 96.7% accuracy at 32× compression versus 40.0% for KVZip+, and report broader gains on LongBench at stronger compression ratios across Qwen3 model sizes. The paper also states that text summarization outperforms Latent Compaction on RULER at the most aggressive ratios and that Phonebook Lookup accuracy approaches zero for all compressed methods at 64× and above. These are author-reported benchmark results. The evaluation counts logical KV pairs; it does not measure actual memory savings or inference speed.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report 96.7% accuracy versus 40.0% for KVZip+ in a highlighted RULER result at 32× compression; they report gains on LongBench at higher ratios across Qwen3 sizes, with non-uniform results by task and compression level.
technical.compute_or_cost: The method performs document-specific test-time optimization, with 1,000 attention-fitting updates per layer and 1,000 joint refinement updates in the reported default. Preparation compute, memory bytes saved, latency and query-throughput changes were not measured in this review; amortization depends on document reuse.
technical.demonstrated_result: The paper documents a two-stage cache-optimization method and benchmark results; its repository is publicly listed under MIT license. No independent execution or reproduction was performed.
technical.implementation_status: Public author repository lists implementation code and an MIT license. No code, model or dataset artifact was downloaded, audited or run.
technical.mechanism: The method initializes a compact document-specific cache using reconstruction-based selection, teacher-attention importance and key-space diversity. A first training stage fits attention outputs and log-normalizers with selected preserver entries fixed; a second jointly optimizes the compact cache by distillation from the full-cache model. Model weights stay frozen and prompts are generic rather than downstream questions.
technical.novelty: Instead of only selecting original KV entries or summarizing a document as text, the method trains a compact document-specific KV representation at test time to approximate the full-cache model’s attention and predictions.
technical.regime: RULER and Phonebook Lookup comparisons use Qwen3-1.7B in Figure 1; LongBench includes Qwen3-0.6B, 1.7B and 4B at 4×–32× compression. Additional retrieval experiments cover other Qwen3 sizes and MiniCPM5, using each model’s own teacher outputs. The paper states logical KV-pair budgets do not establish actual memory savings or inference speedups.
technical.reproducibility: The paper describes training setup and baselines and links code. Independent reproduction, physical cache accounting, serving benchmarks and preparation-cost amortization remain open.
technical.strongest_baseline: KVZip+ is the cited baseline in the highlighted RULER 32× comparison. Baseline ordering is not uniform: the paper says text summarization beats Latent Compaction at the most aggressive RULER ratios; LongBench results favor it over KVZip+ at 16× and 32×.

brief.title: Latent Compaction reports retrieval accuracy gains from document-specific test-time KV-cache training
brief.why_it_matters: If the retrieval results reproduce and preparation cost can be amortized across repeated use of a document, optimizing compact KV state could provide a new option for long-context inference. The current paper establishes benchmark behavior under logical cache budgets, not physical memory reductions, latency gains or serving-cost savings; performance also declines at stronger compression and differs by task.
